topology.target_runs: only the server and its database; no container CPU or memory limits, so the plan size is the limit
topology.driver_runs: SDK workers, load probes, health observer and driver samplers, on a separate host in the target's private network
topology.network: target publishes 8080 only on its private (VPC) address
topology.clock: both hosts NTP-synchronized; latency compares the driver's start time with the server's closed_at

planned_hosts.driver: a separate host in the same VPC with at least 4 vCPU, so client processes are never the limit
planned_hosts.comparison: vultr vhp-4c-8gb-amd runs the rc1 matched profile, unchanged, for continuity with October 20 and 30

ladder.stop_rule: a rate passes when every probe exits 0 (no errors, late or skipped offers, pending work or poll errors), at least 90% of planned workflows close inside the offer window, and the slowest probe's p95 is at most 2 s; a failed rate is repeated once, and two failures end the ladder
ladder.drift_check: the lowest rate again after the ladder

required_evidence: target and driver identity, plan, machine facts and NTP state at both ends
per-step offered, accepted, in-window, completed and verified counts, latencies, errors and verdict
target host CPU (busy, iowait, steal), memory used and available, swap use and traffic, OOM kills and pressure per window
driver host CPU per window, showing the driver was not the limit
ordinary health and ready answers during work and idle waits
target container restarts and OOM kills, database audit and complete teardown
limitations: A development comparison on disposable hosts, not a publishable capacity claim.
One workload cell (one activity, 1 KiB each way); other shapes can saturate differently.
The p95 per step is the slowest probe's p95, not a merged percentile.
Latency crosses two hosts' clocks; NTP offsets of a few milliseconds are small against these latencies but are not removed.
Native rc.2 uses schema 7; it starts from an empty database on every run.
